doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Awards, the NEA Jazz Masters honor and Los Angeles
summary: He recalls being honored in Los Angeles after years away, jokes about the traffic ticket, and says the NEA award surprised him but that awards are political.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Well I was just going to ask you about, you know, you’ve received so many awards, to ask you what they mean to you, particularly the NEA Jazz Masters Award. Do the awards mean anything to you? Is there something else you wanted me to cover? Did I not cover it?

I don’t know. You know, the first time I played LA in a long time was it for the hospital? You know, wasn’t fair to bring in everybody. What’s that hospital out there in Watts? It’s a big thing locally. Anyway, I think it was about three or four years ago we were invited to play, we come back, right. And they -- what’s the name -­
Oh, Maxine was there. Anyway, the other one.
From down there or the one-­
No, down in LA. She’s -- her manager is a wealthy, rich guy. She’s the supervisor.
I’m up in San Francisco. I’m sorry.

Yeah. Well anyway she’s a big wheel. I mean, you know, a big heavyweight, you know. Anyway man, before I played, all these people came on the stage man and gave me all of these awards and I was actually shocked. So they asked me to say something and my exact words, I told them, I said, you know, the only time anybody ever gave me anything here in LA was a traffic ticket.
So I told them how much I really appreciated it. I was shocked man. So I’m trying to ask you a question in regards to the award that -­
The National Endowment for the Arts, Jazz Masters.

I was shocked about that, man. I had no idea. It came as a complete surprise to me but then on the other hand -- which the following year I was on the board, I had to pick somebody and I realized that it’s all political. You don’t have to keep that in but, you know, this is off the record.
